title: Equivalent and Comparing Fractions
seo_title: Grade 4 Equivalent and Comparing Fractions Worksheets (TEKS 4.3C, 4.3D, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.3C determine if two given fractions are equivalent using a variety of methods; 4.3D compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators and represent the comparison using the symbols >, =, or <
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 fraction worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.3C and 4.3D: equivalent fractions with models and multiplying, comparing fractions with models, common denominators and benchmarks, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number to make an equivalent fraction.
key_sub: To compare, use a common denominator or a benchmark like 1/2.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Equivalent fractions name the same amount. Multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 2/3 = 8/12.
  • To compare fractions with different denominators, rename them with a common denominator, or compare each to a benchmark such as 1/2.
  • Use >, < or = to record the comparison. The wholes must be the same size.

Examples

Example

Compare 3/4 and 5/8.

3/4 = 6/8

6/8 > 5/8

Answer: 3/4 > 5/8

Example

Compare 2/5 and 7/10 using 1/2.

2/5 is less than 1/2.

7/10 is more than 1/2.

Answer: 2/5 < 7/10

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying only the denominatorMultiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
Thinking 1/8 > 1/4 because 8 > 4More parts means smaller parts.
Comparing only the numerators of 3/4 and 3/8 the wrong wayWith the same numerator, the smaller denominator is the bigger fraction.

faq.a: Determine if two fractions are equivalent using a variety of methods.

faq.q: How do you find a common denominator?
faq.a: Find a number that both denominators divide into, such as 12 for 3 and 4. Then rename both fractions.
Easy fractions like 0, 1/2 and 1 that help you compare. 3/8 is less than 1/2, and 5/6 is more than 1/2.

items.q: Divide the top and bottom of 1012 by 2. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide both numbers by 2: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 12 ÷ 2 = 6. So 1012 = 56. The parts are bigger, but there are fewer of them.

items.q: Divide the top and bottom of 412 by 4. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide both numbers by 4: 4 ÷ 4 = 1 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. So 412 = 13. The parts are bigger, but there are fewer of them.

items.q: Divide the top and bottom of 610 by 2. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide both numbers by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 10 ÷ 2 = 5. So 610 = 35. The parts are bigger, but there are fewer of them.

items.q: Divide the top and bottom of 75100 by 25. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide both numbers by 25: 75 ÷ 25 = 3 and 100 ÷ 25 = 4. So 75100 = 34. The parts are bigger, but there are fewer of them.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 35?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number: 3 × 2 = 6 and 5 × 2 = 10, so 35 = 610. Adding the same number, or multiplying only one number, gives a different amount.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 23?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number: 2 × 4 = 8 and 3 × 4 = 12, so 23 = 812. Adding the same number, or multiplying only one number, gives a different amount.

items.q: 13 of bar A is shaded. 12 of bar B is shaded. Gabriel says the picture shows 13 > 12. What is wrong?
c: Gabriel should count the white parts.
Bar A has more parts, so it wins.
Nothing. 13 > 12.
items.e: You can only compare fractions of the same whole. Bar A is longer than bar B, so 13 of A can look longer than 12 of B. With the same whole, 13 < 12.

items.q: 38 of bar A is shaded. 12 of bar B is shaded. Marcus says the picture shows 38 > 12. What is wrong?
c: Marcus should count the white parts.
Bar A has more parts, so it wins.
Nothing. 38 > 12.
items.e: You can only compare fractions of the same whole. Bar A is longer than bar B, so 38 of A can look longer than 12 of B. With the same whole, 38 < 12.

items.q: 14 of circle A is shaded. 12 of circle B is shaded. Does this picture show that 14 > 12?
c: No. The circles are different sizes.
Yes. The shaded part of A is bigger.
No. They show the same amount.
items.e: No. Circle A is a much bigger whole than circle B, so the pictures cannot be compared. With the same whole, 14 < 12: one of 4 equal pieces is smaller than one of 2 equal pieces.

sets.title: Compare with common denominators and benchmarks

items.q:
Find the missing number.
23 = ?12
items.e: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so multiply the top and the bottom by 4: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 = 812. (Adding the same number to the top and bottom does not keep the fraction the same.)

items.q:
Find the missing number.
34 = ?12
items.e: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so multiply the top and the bottom by 3: 3 × 3 = 9. So 34 = 912. (Adding the same number to the top and bottom does not keep the fraction the same.)

items.q:
Find the missing number.
56 = ?12
items.e: 12 ÷ 6 = 2, so multiply the top and the bottom by 2: 5 × 2 = 10. So 56 = 1012. (Adding the same number to the top and bottom does not keep the fraction the same.)

items.q:
Find the missing number.
35 = ?10
items.e: 10 ÷ 5 = 2, so multiply the top and the bottom by 2: 3 × 2 = 6. So 35 = 610. (Adding the same number to the top and bottom does not keep the fraction the same.)

items.q:

items.e: 100 ÷ 10 = 10, so multiply the top and the bottom by 10: 7 × 10 = 70. So 710 = 70100. (Adding the same number to the top and bottom does not keep the fraction the same.)

items.q:

34 = ?8
items.e: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so multiply the top and the bottom by 2: 3 × 2 = 6. So 34 = 68. (Adding the same number to the top and bottom does not keep the fraction the same.)

items.q: Which number can be a common denominator for 34 and 56?
items.e: A common denominator must be a multiple of both 4 and 6. 12 = 4 × 3 and 12 = 6 × 2. Adding the denominators (10) does not work.

items.q: Which number can be a common denominator for 12 and 35?
items.e: A common denominator must be a multiple of both 2 and 5. 10 = 2 × 5 and 10 = 5 × 2. Adding the denominators (7) does not work.

items.q: Which number can be a common denominator for 23 and 34?
items.e: A common denominator must be a multiple of both 3 and 4. 12 = 3 × 4 and 12 = 4 × 3. Adding the denominators (7) does not work.

items.q: Which number can be a common denominator for 310 and 47100?
items.e: A common denominator must be a multiple of both 10 and 100. 100 = 10 × 10 and 100 = 100 × 1. Adding the denominators (110) does not work.

items.q: Where is 58?
items.e: Half of 8 is 4. 5 is more than 4, so 58 is more than 12. It is less than 1 because 5 is less than 8.

items.q: Where is 38?
items.e: Half of 8 is 4. 3 is less than 4, so 38 is less than 12.

items.q: Where is 612?
items.e: Half of 12 is 6, so 612 is exactly 12.

items.q: Where is 410?
items.e: Half of 10 is 5. 4 is less than 5, so 410 is less than 12.

items.q: Where is 712?
items.e: Half of 12 is 6. 7 is more than 6, so 712 is more than 12. It is less than 1 because 7 is less than 12.

items.q: Where is 76?
items.e: The top number (7) is bigger than the bottom number (6), so 76 is more than 1 whole: 66 = 1 and 16 more.

items.q: Compare 38 and 46. Which statement is true?
c: 46 < 38
38 = 46
38 < 46
38 > 46
items.e: Use 12 as a benchmark. Half of 8 is 4. 3 is less than 4, so 38 is less than 12. Half of 6 is 3. 4 is more than 3, so 46 is more than 12. So 38 < 46.

items.q: Compare 25 and 712. Which statement is true?
c: 712 < 25
25 = 712
25 > 712
25 < 712
items.e: Use 12 as a benchmark. Double the top: 2 × 2 = 4, which is less than 5, so 25 is less than 12. Half of 12 is 6. 7 is more than 6, so 712 is more than 12. So 25 < 712.

items.q: Compare 56 and 410. Which statement is true?
c: 56 > 410
56 < 410
56 = 410
410 > 56
items.e: Use 12 as a benchmark. Half of 6 is 3. 5 is more than 3, so 56 is more than 12. Half of 10 is 5. 4 is less than 5, so 410 is less than 12. So 56 > 410.

items.q: Compare 34 and 512. Which statement is true?
c: 34 = 512
34 > 512
34 < 512
512 > 34
items.e: Use 12 as a benchmark. Half of 4 is 2. 3 is more than 2, so 34 is more than 12. Half of 12 is 6. 5 is less than 6, so 512 is less than 12. So 34 > 512.

items.q: Isabella ran 34 of a mile. Harper ran 23 of a mile. Who ran farther?
items.e: Write both in twelfths: 34 = 912 and 23 = 812. 9 is greater than 8, so 34 > 23. Isabella ran farther.

items.q: Recipe A uses 34 cup of flour. Recipe B uses 58 cup of flour. Which recipe uses more flour?
items.e: Write both in eighths: 34 = 68. 6 is greater than 5, so 34 > 58. Recipe A uses more flour.

items.q: Ava and Elijah each painted a fence. The fences are the same size. Ava painted 35 of a fence and Elijah painted 410. Who painted more?
items.e: Write both in tenths: 35 = 610. 6 is greater than 4, so 35 > 410. Ava painted more.

items.q: Ximena has read 512 of a book. Sofia has read 12 of the same book. Who has read more of it?
items.e: Use 12 as a benchmark. Half of 12 is 6. 5 is less than 6, so 512 is less than 12. Sofia has read more.

items.q: Caleb drank 710 of a bottle of water. Emma drank 45 of the same kind of bottle. Who drank more?
items.e: Write both in tenths: 45 = 810. 7 is less than 8, so 710 < 45. Emma drank more.

items.q: Mateo walked 23 of a mile to school. Grace walked 812 of a mile. Who walked farther?
items.e: Write both in twelfths: 23 = 812. Both are 812, so 23 = 812. They walked the same distance.

items.q: Jar A has 610 liter of juice. Jar B has 58100 liter of juice. Which jar has more juice?
items.e: Write both in hundredths: 610 = 60100. 60 is greater than 58, so 610 > 58100. Jar A has more juice.

items.q: Isaac spent 56 of an hour on homework. Carlos spent 78 of an hour. Who spent more time?
items.e: Each fraction is 1 piece away from 1 whole. 56 is missing 16, and 78 is missing 18. 18 is the smaller missing piece, so 78 is closer to 1 hour. Carlos spent more time.

items.q: A green ribbon is 45 yard long. A blue ribbon is 710 yard long. Which ribbon is longer?
items.e: Write both in tenths: 45 = 810. 8 is greater than 7, so 45 > 710. The green ribbon is longer.

items.q: Liam hiked 512 of a trail. Aaliyah hiked 38 of the same trail. Who hiked farther?
items.e: Write both in 24ths: 512 = 1024 and 38 = 924. 10 is greater than 9, so 512 > 38. Liam hiked farther.

items.q: Gabriel ate 24 of a pizza. Harper ate 48 of a pizza of the same size. Who ate more?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom of 24 by 2: 24 = 48. Harper ate more slices, but they were smaller, so they ate the same amount.

items.q: Zoe ate 23 of a pizza. Camila ate 46 of a pizza of the same size. Who ate more?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom of 23 by 2: 23 = 46. Camila ate more slices, but they were smaller, so they ate the same amount.

items.q: Isaac ate 34 of a pizza. Carlos ate 58 of a pizza of the same size. Who ate more?
items.e: Change 34 to eighths: multiply the top and bottom by 2 to get 68. 68 is more than 58, so Isaac ate more.

items.q: Mia ate 26 of a pizza. Luis ate 412 of a pizza of the same size. Who ate more?
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom of 26 by 2: 26 = 412. Luis ate more slices, but they were smaller, so they ate the same amount.

items.q: A recipe needs 34 cup of milk. Mateo only has a 18 cup scoop. How many scoops does he need?
items.e: 34 = 68, because 3 × 2 = 6 and 4 × 2 = 8. So he needs 6 scoops of 18 cup.

items.q: A recipe needs 12 cup of milk. Liam only has a 14 cup scoop. How many scoops does he need?
items.e: 12 = 24, because 1 × 2 = 2 and 2 × 2 = 4. So he needs 2 scoops of 14 cup.

items.q: A recipe needs 23 cup of milk. Lucia only has a 16 cup scoop. How many scoops does she need?
items.e: 23 = 46, because 2 × 2 = 4 and 3 × 2 = 6. So she needs 4 scoops of 16 cup.

items.q: A recipe needs 12 cup of milk. Ava only has a 18 cup scoop. How many scoops does she need?
items.e: 12 = 48, because 1 × 4 = 4 and 2 × 4 = 8. So she needs 4 scoops of 18 cup.

items.q: A dime is 110 of a dollar. A penny is 1100 of a dollar. Ethan has 3 dimes. What fraction of a dollar is that, in hundredths?
items.e: 3 dimes are 310 of a dollar. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 30100. That is 30 cents.

items.q: Noah has 70 pennies, which is 70100 of a dollar. He trades them for dimes. How many dimes does he get?
items.e: 70100 = 710: divide the top and bottom by 10. Each dime is 110 of a dollar, so he gets 7 dimes.
